en: (Incomplete) Oṃ, salutation to the Gurus beginning with Śiva; salutation to the Goddess Śrī Kubjikā.
Now follows the worship of the western deity, performed with devotion toward the circle of gurus.
The *balikoṭa* is a long quadrangle with its corners bent; the *arghapātra* is a triangle.
In the mandala of the water-vessel, *vauṣaṭ*, [perform] the bath.
Aiṃ: Bathing, sandals, sandalwood paste, vermilion, flowers, and sipping water (ācamana).
Aiṃ Hrāṃ, svāhā to the principle of the self (ātmatattva). Aiṃ Hrīṃ, svāhā to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva).
Aiṃ Hrūṃ, svāhā to the principle of Śiva.
Homage to the Guru.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃḥ.
Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom that state was revealed— the state which is of the form of an unbroken circle and by which all that is moving and unmoving is pervaded.
The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the divine Maheśvara;
the Guru is the entire universe—salutations to that illustrious Guru.
Aiṃ. Salutations to the supreme gurus. Salutations to the gurus who abide in the highest place.
Salutation to the supreme teachers and gurus.
Aiṃ, to the seat of the argha vessel; to the lotus seat; to the seat of the water vessel.
Ātma-aiṃ, the sandals for the tortoise-seat.
Kiṇi vicce koṅkaṇāyai hraḥ astrāya phaṭ. [To] Lātine.
Rotate the vajra-mudrā three times on the forehead: Aiṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Vajrapañjare Svāhā.
The purification of the ten gates.
Aiṃ cala makule kulamacale aiṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
The ritual placement (nyāsa).
Kiṇi vicce koṅkaṇāyai hraḥ astrāya phaṭ.
The purification of the hands.
Aiṃ! Salutation to the Blessed One, the Lady of the Heart-Lotus; Hrāṃ Śrī(-)! Salutation to the two thumbs.
Hsphreṁ, to Kubjikā, the lamp of the Kula, Hrīṁ, to the two index fingers, svāhā!
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, O you with the dark-red crest, hrūṃ; to the two middle fingers, vaṣaṭ!
Ghorā, Aghorā, Aghorāmukhī, Bahurūpā; Hraiṃ, to the two ring fingers, Hūṃ.
Chāṃ chīṃ, to Mahantārikā; hrauṃ, to the two little fingers (kaniṣṭhā), vauṣaṭ.
*Kiṇi vicce koṅkaṇāyai hraḥ astrāya phaṭ*, [and] *pādukām* for the back of the hand; thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the hands.
Aiṃ! Salutation to the Blessed One, to the Lotus of the Heart; Hrāṃ! To the upward-facing face, the sandals.
Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā, the lamp of the Kula; Hrīṃ, to the eastern face preceded by Śrī.
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, O you with the dark-red crest, hrūṃ! To the glorious right face.
To the one who is Ghora, Aghora, and Aghorāmukhī, to the multiformed one, Hraiṃ, to the venerable northern face.
Chāṃ chīṃ to Mahantārikā; hrauṃ to the venerable Western Face.
Kiṇi vicce koṅkaṇāyai hraḥ, [obeisance] to the venerable Parāparavaktra.
Thus is the placement of the face.
Aiṃ! Salutation to the Blessed One, to the Lotus of the Heart; Hrāṃ! Salutation to the Śrī-hṛdaya.
Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā, the lamp of the Kula, Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, O you with the dark-red crest! Hrūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest.
Ghora, Aghora, Aghorāmukhī, Bahurūpā; Hraiṃ, for the glorious armor, Hūṃ!
Chāṃ chīṃ, obeisance to Mahantārikā; hrauṃ, obeisance with the vaṣaṭ-call to the three eyes of Śrī.
Kiṇi vicce koṅkaṇāyai hraḥ astrāya phaṭ.
Thus is the ritual placement of the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*).
The worship of the water vessel: Aiṃ, the pādukā for the seat of the water vessel.
Hskṣmlvryūṃ, to the venerable Śkṣmlvryīṃ, the Goddess of the Water Vessel (Śrījalapātrabhaṭṭārikā), the consort of Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda, the Lord of Heroes (Vīrādhipati), [I offer] the sandals.
Having worshipped with the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga), beginning with "Hrāṃ, obeisance to the heart," and so forth.
After performing the invocation and other rites, one should display the Dhenu-mudrā. [Then recite] the Gāyatrī.
Aiṃ! We know Kubjikā; we meditate upon her who is the lamp of the Kula; may that Kubjī inspire us.
With that mantra, sprinkle all substances with water; one should also pour it over one's own head.
The sandals for the seat of the argha vessel.
Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ! Flash forth! O you of terrible and most radiant form, move, move intensely! Speak! Vomit! Subdue! Strike down! Destroy! O destroyer of obstacles! Hūṃ phaṭ!
To the sandals of the venerable Komārikā Vicce!
ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ, to Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda Virādhipati; HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ, to the venerable Śrī-arghapātra-bhaṭṭārikā.
Having worshipped with "Hrāṃ, obeisance to the heart" and so forth, one should perform the invocation and other rites and display the yoni-mudrā.
Taking the flower situated in the *argha* vessel with the tortoise gesture (*kacchapa-mudrā*), one should perform the purification of the elements (*bhūta-śuddhi*).
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃḥ. With this mantra, one should perform [the rite] both in the direct and reverse order of the syllables.
Thus ends the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
Then follows the self-worship.
Aiṃ: unguent and sandals. Hrīṃ: the three principles and unbroken rice grains.
Śrīṃ Vīrabhadra! Hsphreṃ, the Enchantress of all people!
Hsauṁ: the flower-adornment of various parasols.
Hskṣmlvryūṃ, to Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda, the Lord of Viras; Śkṣmlvryīṃ, to the form of the Self (Ātmamūrti). Kusaum, the sandals! One should sprinkle the three points upon the head.
Invocation.
Aiṃ! Within the circle of the venerable Saṃvarta, the most formidable power of bliss, accompanied by the stages of the Krama, performs the emission.
Therein are four groups according to the rule: one consisting of Akula and Kula, another of five, and yet another of six;
these four—
Furthermore, he who is conjoined with the fourfold reality that is five-fold and more, and with the maṇḍala— homage to that excellent guru, Bhairava, the illustrious Kujeśa.
Aiṃ! I invoke this; I invoke.
Salutation to the primordial deity, the infinite mandala.
Hskṣmlvryūṃ Ā Śkṣmlvryīṃ Pā.
The three gods.
To Narāsana; to Mayūrāsana; to Mūṣāsana.
Bali for the goddess Dambhakī and the kṣetrapāla Mahādhvāṅkṣa at Prastaradvīpa.
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, to Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha, [this is] the offering (pā) and the sacrificial oblation (bali).
Gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaḥ glauṃ, to Kulagaṇeśvara, [this] offering (bali).
After the invocation and other rites, one should display the staff, the threatening gesture, and the elephant mudrās.
Aiṃ, to the lotus seat. Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, to the venerable Śrītriśuddhibhaṭṭārikā, the sovereign of heroes, Bhairavānanda, the power of bliss, Śkṣmlvryīṃ. This is the offering.
Aiṃ, obeisance to the lotus posture; obeisance to the human posture.
Hrūṃ! To the Lord of Heroes, Bhairavānanda, the power of bliss, Srūṃ! To the venerable Navātman, the Guru-maṇḍala, I worship the sandals.
Threefold: the offering (bali), the yoni-mudrā.
Homage to Śrīnātha! Homage to Śrīsiddhinātha! Homage to Śrīkujeśanātha! Na Khaḥ, Vaṣaṭ! Hraiṃ, to the armor, Hūṃ! Hrauṃ, to the three eyes, Vauṣaṭ!
Hraḥ, to the weapon, Phaṭ!
Having thus worshipped the six limbs,
and having recited "hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ" eight times, and having offered three handfuls of flowers with that same mantra,
one should take that vessel with both hands and [recite] "hrīṃ haṃ saḥ mārttaṇḍabhairavāya".

Having offered the water for the guest-offering (arghya) to the Sun with the mantra: "To Him who is endowed with the power of illumination, this arghya, svāhā," one should sprinkle the door with the water from that arghya while reciting "hrīṃ namaḥ" and perform the worship of the door.
In the absence of a door, one should worship after mentally conceiving a door.
Now follows the worship of the doors.
On an udumbara tree facing upward.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ Gāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati.
To his right:
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ Maṃ, salutation to Mahālakṣmī.
To her left:
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ Hsauṁ Saṁ, obeisance to Sarasvatī. On the right branch:
Aiṃ Gāṃ, salutation to Gaṇeśa. On the left branch.
Aiṃ Kṣāṃ, salutation to Kṣetrapāla; [at] both sides of the door.
Aiṁ vāṁ, obeisance to Vaṭuka. Aiṁ gaṁ, obeisance to Gaṅgā.
Aiṁ yāṁ, obeisance to the Yoginī. Aiṁ yaṁ, obeisance to Yamunā.
Below, salutation to the weapon-mantra (astra).

If one is unable [to perform the full ritual], one should worship with "Aiṃ, obeisance to the deities presiding over the doors, beginning with Gaṇeśa," and then enter the house of worship, preceded by the left foot.
Aiṁ Oṃ rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. With this, one should purify the ground for worship.
Then, in the southwest: having worshipped with "Aiṁ Oṃ, obeisance to Vāstupuruṣa" and "Aiṁ Oṃ,

obeisance to Brahmā," and having dispelled the celestial obstacles while surveying with divine vision using the root mantra, one should dispel the atmospheric obstacles with water while reciting "Hrīṁ, to the weapon, Phaṭ."

Having dispelled the terrestrial obstacles by striking the ground three times with the left heel while saying "phaṭ," and having consecrated the unhusked grain seven times while saying "aiṃ phaṭ," [he recites]:
"Oṃ, may those beings depart who dwell upon the earth."
May those beings who create obstacles perish by the command of Śiva.
Thus, one should scatter unbroken grains in the four directions.
Then, having worshipped the seat with "Aiṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to the Support-Power (Ādhāraśakti), the Lotus-Seated One," [one recites]:
"Oṃ, for the acceptance of the seat, Merupṛṣṭha is the Seer (Ṛṣi), Sutala is the Metre (Chandas), and Kūrma is the Deity;
this is the application (Viniyoga)."
Oṃ! O Earth, by you the worlds are supported; O Goddess, you are supported by Viṣṇu.
May you support me always; make this seat pure.
Having recited this, one should sit down in the sequence beginning with the svastika posture.
Then, with palms joined in the *puṭāñjali* gesture, [one should offer salutations] on the left:
*Oṃ gurubhyo namaḥ*; *Oṃ paramagurubhyo namaḥ*; *Oṃ parāparagurubhyo namaḥ*; *Oṃ parameṣṭhigurubhyo namaḥ*.
To the south: *oṃ gaṇeśāya namaḥ*. In the center: *oṃ śrīṃ siddhilakṣmyai devatāyai namaḥ*.

Then, having purified both hands with perfume and flowers while reciting *hsauṃ hūṃ phaṭ*, and having performed the triple *tāla* strike upward with *hrīṃ astrāya phaṭ*, one should perform the binding of the directions (*digbandhana*) with snapping fingers while reciting *phaṭ*.
"Oṃ hūṃ phaṭ rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Having performed self-protection with this mantra, one should perform the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
Now follows the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
Having visualized a rampart of fire with the syllable *vaṃ* and a stream of water,

and having placed the two hands palms-upward on one's lap, one should visualize the individual soul (*jīvātman*) in the form of a lamp-flame within the center of the heart-lotus while reciting *so'haṃ*. Then, by means of the *yonimudrā* while reciting *aiṃ*, one should contemplate the *kuṇḍalinī* at the *mūlādhāra*.
Uttering "Hūṃ," one should raise Kuṇḍalinī and, together with the individual soul (jīvātman),

cause her to pierce the six cakras known as Mūlādhāra, Svādhiṣṭhāna, Maṇipūraka, Anāhata, Viśuddha, and Ājñā along the path of the Suṣumnā, reaching the thousand-petalled lotus situated at the head and facing downward.

Having joined each of these to the Supreme Self situated within the pericarp (*karṇikā*), one should likewise [join] therein the twenty-four principles (*tattva*): earth, water, fire, air, ether; smell, taste, form, touch, sound; the nose, tongue, eyes, skin, ears; speech, hands, feet, anus, genitals; primordial nature (*prakṛti*), mind (*manas*), intellect (*buddhi*), and ego (*ahaṃkāra*).
Having contemplated the sluggish [state], one should visualize the seed-syllable *yaṃ*, smoke-colored, in the left nostril;
by reciting it sixteen times, one fills the body with air, holds both nostrils,
and performs *kumbhaka* (retention) by reciting that same syllable sixty-four times.
Having dried up the body together with the black-colored person of sin (pāpapuruṣa) residing in the left side of the abdomen,
one should exhale the air through the right nostril while reciting [the mantra] thirty-two times.
Then, having meditated on the seed-syllable of fire, *raṃ*, red in color, within the right nostril,
one should fill the body by reciting it sixteen times; holding the nostrils,
one should perform the *kuṃbhaka* (retention) by reciting it sixty-four times, thereby burning the body along with the personification of sin.
By reciting [the mantra] thirty-two times, one should exhale the breath through the left nostril along with the ashes.
Then, having meditated on the lunar seed-syllable *ṭhaṃ*, white in color, at the left nostril,
one should lead the moon to the forehead by reciting it sixteen times; then, holding the two nostrils,
one should extract that moon from the forehead by reciting the Varuṇa seed-syllable *vaṃ* sixty-four times.
Having fashioned the entire body with white lime consisting of the letters of the *mātṛkā*,
one should contemplate the body as very firm by reciting the seed-syllable of earth (*laṃ*) thirty-two times, and then exhale the air through the right [nostril].
Then, having united the individual soul (jīvātman) with Paraśiva by means of the mantra "Haṃ Saḥ," one should lead [the soul] back to its proper place by means of the mantra "So 'ham."

Then follows the installation of the vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*). Having visualized one’s chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*) in the form of the power of life (*prāṇaśakti*) within the root mantra, and having touched the heart with the *lelihāna* mudrā, [one recites]: *Āṃ kroṃ hrīṃ haṃ saḥ, my vital breaths (*prāṇāḥ*) are here as vital breaths; Āṃ kroṃ hrīṃ haṃ saḥ, my life-force (*jīva*) is established here.*
Āṃ kroṃ hrīṃ haṃ saḥ! May all my senses—Āṃ kroṃ hrīṃ haṃ saḥ!—as well as my speech, mind, eyes, ears, nose, and vital breaths, come here and remain happily for a long time; svāhā!
Then, with the mantra "Oṃ Āḥ So'haṃ," one should contemplate one's own body as consisting of light.
Then follows the placement of the Mātṛkās (the alphabet).

Oṃ. Of this Mātṛkā-mantra, Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), Mātṛkā-Sarasvatī is the deity (devatā), the consonants are the seeds (bījas), the vowels are the powers (śaktis), the Unmanifest is the bolt (kīlaka), and its application (viniyoga) is in the ritual placement of the letters (lipinyāsa).
Then follows the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the seers and so forth: On the head: *namaḥ* to Brahmā, the seer (*ṛṣi*).

In the mouth: *namaḥ* to Gāyatrī, the meter (*chandas*). In the heart: *namaḥ* to Mātṛkā-Sarasvatī, the deity (*devatā*). In the secret place: *namaḥ* to the seed-syllables (*bīja*) beginning with *ha*. In the feet: *namaḥ* to the vowels (*svara*), which are the powers (*śakti*).
Salutation to the unmanifested Kīlaka in all limbs.
Now follow the ritual assignments (nyāsa) for the hands and limbs.
Aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ, salutation to the two thumbs (aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ).
iṁ caṁ chaṁ jaṁ jhaṁ ñaṁ īṁ, svāhā to the two index fingers.
uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ, to the two middle fingers, vaṣaṭ; eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ, to the two ring fingers, hūṃ;
oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ auṃ, to the two little fingers, vauṣaṭ.
Aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ aḥ, phaṭ with both palms and backs of the hands.
Aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ, homage to the heart (hṛdayāya namaḥ).
Iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ, svāhā to the head (śirase svāhā).
Uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhāyai vaṣaṭ).
Eṃ Taṃ Thaṃ Daṃ Dhaṃ Naṃ Aiṃ, for the armor (kavaca), Hūṃ.
Oṃ Paṃ Phaṃ Baṃ Bhaṃ Maṃ Auṃ, for the three eyes (netratraya), Vauṣaṭ.
Aṃ Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Vaṃ Śaṃ Ṣaṃ Saṃ Haṃ Laṃ Kṣaṃ Aḥ, for the weapon (astra), Phaṭ.
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the final *mātṛkā*.
In the *ādhāra*, the *liṅga*, the navel, the heart-lotus, the root of the palate, and the forehead;
in the two-petaled, sixteen-petaled, twenty-two-petaled, ten-petaled, twelve-petaled, and four-petaled [lotuses];
at the end of the abode (*vāsānta*), in the middle of the hair, and in the region of the throat accompanied by the letters *ḍa*, *pha*, *ka*, and *ṭha*—[therein reside] the vowels.
The one of pure intellect should place the two *hakṣa* syllables in the middle of the bow for the sake of attaining perfection through the realization of the ritual placement (*nyāsa*).
Having meditated thus: *aṃ namaḥ*, *āṃ namaḥ*, *iṃ namaḥ*, *īṃ namaḥ*, *uṃ namaḥ*, *ūṃ namaḥ*, *ṛṃ namaḥ*, *ṝṃ namaḥ*,
*ḷṃ namaḥ*, *ḹṃ namaḥ*, *eṃ namaḥ*, *aiṃ namaḥ*, *oṃ namaḥ*, *auṃ namaḥ*.
Aṃ, homage! Aḥ, homage!
Thus, one should place [the mantra] upon the sixteen-petaled lotus at the throat.
Kaṃ namaḥ | Khaṃ namaḥ | Gaṃ namaḥ | Ghaṃ namaḥ | Ṅaṃ namaḥ | Caṃ namaḥ | Chaṃ namaḥ | Jaṃ namaḥ | Jhaṃ namaḥ | Ñaṃ namaḥ | Ṭaṃ namaḥ | Ṭhaṃ namaḥ ||
Thus, one should place [the mantra] upon the twelve-petaled lotus in the heart.
Ḍaṃ namaḥ | Ḍhaṃ namaḥ | Ṇaṃ namaḥ | Taṃ namaḥ | Thaṃ namaḥ | Daṃ namaḥ | Dhaṃ namaḥ | Naṃ namaḥ | Paṃ namaḥ | Phaṃ namaḥ |
Thus, one should place [the syllables] upon the ten-petalled lotus at the navel.
Baṃ namaḥ | Bhaṃ namaḥ | Maṃ namaḥ | Yaṃ namaḥ | Raṃ namaḥ | Laṃ namaḥ ||
Thus, one should place [the syllables] in the six-petalled lotus called the base of the linga (the *maṇipūra*).
Vaṃ, obeisance! Śaṃ, obeisance! Ṣaṃ, obeisance! Saṃ, obeisance!
Thus, one should place [the syllables] upon the four-petaled lotus at the *mūlādhāra*.
Haṃ namaḥ | Kṣaṃ namaḥ. Thus one should place [these] upon the two-petaled lotus between the eyebrows.
Then follows the external placement of the Mātṛkās.
Meditative absorption.
Her face, arms, waist, and chest are adorned with the fifty letters of the alphabet;
she wears a radiant crown bound with the crescent moon; her breasts are full and lofty;
and with her lotus-like hands, she holds a mudrā, a rosary, a jar brimming with nectar, and the Vidyā.
I take refuge in the Goddess of Speech, who bears a lute, possesses pure radiance, and has three eyes.
Having meditated thus, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa).

Aṃ, salutation to the forehead; Āṃ, salutation to the mouth; Iṃ, salutation to the right eye; Īṃ, salutation to the left eye; Uṃ, salutation to the right ear; Ūṃ, salutation to the left ear; Ṛṃ, salutation to the right nostril; Ṝṃ, salutation to the left nostril.
Ḷaṃ, salutation to the right cheek; Ḷīṃ, salutation to the left cheek; Eṃ, salutation to the upper lip; Aiṃ, salutation to the lower lip;
Oṃ, salutation to the upper teeth; Auṃ, salutation to the lower teeth;
Aṃ, salutation to the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra); Aḥ, salutation to the mouth; Kaṃ, salutation to the root of the right arm.
*Khaṃ* namaḥ to the left elbow; *gaṃ* namaḥ to the left wrist; *ghaṃ* namaḥ to the base of the fingers;

*ṅaṃ* namaḥ to the tips of the fingers; *caṃ* namaḥ to the root of the left arm; *chaṃ* namaḥ to the left elbow; *jaṃ* namaḥ to the left wrist; *jhaṃ* namaḥ to the base of the left fingers; *ñaṃ* namaḥ...

Ṭaṃ namaḥ on the tip of the left toe; ṭhaṃ namaḥ at the base of the right foot; ḍaṃ namaḥ on the shank; ḍhaṃ namaḥ on the ankle; ṇaṃ namaḥ on the tip of the toes of the [right] foot; taṃ namaḥ at the base of the left foot; thaṃ namaḥ on the left shank; daṃ namaḥ on the left knee.
*Dhaṃ*—salutation to the left temple; *naṃ*—salutation to the tips of the toes of the left foot;

*paṃ*—salutation to the right side; *phaṃ*—salutation to the left side; *baṃ*—salutation to the back; *bhaṃ*—salutation to the navel; *maṃ*—salutation to the abdomen; *yaṃ*—salutation to the heart; *raṃ*—salutation to the right shoulder.

*Laṃ*, homage to the left shoulder; *vaṃ*, homage to the hump of the neck; *śaṃ*, homage from the heart to the right hand; *ṣaṃ*, homage from the heart to the left hand; *saṃ*, homage from the heart to the right foot; *haṃ*, homage from the heart to the left foot; *laṃ*, homage from the heart to the abdomen; *kṣaṃ*, homage from the heart to the mouth.
In all cases, one should place [the mantra] beginning with the seed-syllable of Śrī and ending with "namaḥ."
Then follows the placement of the seats (pīṭhanyāsa): in the heart.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ, salutation to the Support-Energy (Ādhāraśakti). Aiṃ, salutation to the Tortoise (Kūrma). Aiṃ, to Ananta. Aiṃ, to the Earth. Aiṃ, to the Ocean of Milk. Aiṃ, to the Seven Islands. Aiṃ, to the Jewel-Pavilion (Maṇimaṇḍapa).
Aiṁ, to the wish-fulfilling tree; Aiṁ, to the jeweled lion throne.
Aiṁ to Dharma on the right shoulder; Aiṁ to Jñāna on the left shoulder;
Aiṁ to Vairāgya on the left thigh; Aiṁ to Aiśvarya on the right thigh;
Aiṁ to Adharma on the face; Aiṁ to Ajñāna on the left side.
Aiṃ at the navel for the sake of non-detachment; Aiṃ on the right side for the sake of non-sovereignty.
Again, in the heart: Aiṃ to Ananta; Aiṃ to the Lotus; Aiṃ Aṃ to the Solar Orb consisting of twelve kalās; Aiṃ Uṃ to the Lunar Orb consisting of sixteen kalās.
Aiṃ Maṃ, salutation to the fire-mandala consisting of ten kalās. Aiṃ Saṃ, salutation to Sattva. Aiṃ Raṃ, salutation to Rajas. Aiṃ Taṃ, salutation to Tamas. Aiṃ Āṃ, salutation to the Self (Ātman).
Aiṃ Aṃ, salutation to the Inner Self (Antarātman). Aiṃ Paṃ, salutation to the Supreme Self (Paramātman). Aiṃ Hrīṃ, salutation to the Self of Knowledge (Jñānātman).
In the center of the heart-lotus and upon its filaments.
Aiṁ to Jayā; Aiṁ to Vijayā; Aiṁ to Ajitā; Aiṁ to Aparājitā; Aiṁ to Nityā; Aiṁ to Vilāsinī; Aiṁ to Dogdhrī; Aiṁ to Aghorā;
Aiṁ to Maṅgalā. In the pericarp: Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ to Padmāsana.
Then, having performed three breath-retentions (prāṇāyāma) with the root-bīja, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the seer (ṛṣi) and the other [limbs].

Aiṃ. Of this Siddhilakṣmī mantra, Trilocana is the seer (ṛṣi), Jagatī is the meter (chandaḥ), Śrīsiddhilakṣmī is the deity (devatā), Śrīṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja), Hrīṃ is the power (śakti), Hūṃ is the pin (kīlaka), and its application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of the four aims of human life. Salutation to the seer Trilocana on the head; salutation to the Jagatī meter in the mouth.
Homage! Homage to the deity Siddhilakṣmī in the heart; homage to the seed-syllable Śrīṃ in the secret place; homage to the power Hrīṃ in the two feet; homage to the pin Hūṃ in all limbs.
Then follow the ritual placements on the hands and limbs (karāṅganyāsa).
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ Oṃ Paramahaṃsini, salutation with the two thumbs (aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ). Aiṃ Oṃ Nirvāṇamārgade Devi, Svāhā with the two index fingers (tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā).
Aiṃ Oṃ Viṣamopaplavaśamani, Vaṣaṭ with the two middle fingers (madhyamābhyāṃ vaṣaṭ).
Aiṁ Oṃ, O destroyer of all misfortunes, calamities, and afflictions; Hūṃ to the two ring fingers.
Aiṃ Oṃ, O ferry across the ocean of all calamities; Vauṣaṭ to the two little fingers.
Aiṃ Oṃ! O destroyer of all enemies, O subduer! Phaṭ with both palms and backs of the hands!
Aiṁ Oṃ, obeisance to the Heart of the Supreme Swan (Paramahaṃsinī).
Aiṁ Oṃ, obeisance to the Head of the Goddess who bestows the path to Nirvāṇa. Aiṁ Oṃ, Vaṣaṭ to the Crest-lock (Śikhā) that pacifies calamities and misfortunes.
Aiṁ Oṃ, to the armor that shatters all misfortunes, calamities, and afflictions, Hūṃ!
Aiṁ Oṃ, to the three eyes that ferry one across the ocean of all calamities, Vauṣaṭ! Aiṁ Oṃ, to the weapon that destroys all enemies, Phaṭ!
Then follows the placement upon the faces.
In the eastern face:
*aiṃ aiṃ namaḥ sarvasiddhiyoginībhyaḥ*, obeisance to the eastern face. In the southern face: [aiṃ aiṃ namaḥ sarvasiddhiyoginībhyaḥ].
Aiṃ Aiṃ, salutation to the Mothers of all Siddhis; salutation to the Tatpuruṣa face.
Aiṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ! Salutation to the southern face, Aghoravaktra, who is delighted by eternal, ever-arisen bliss.
In the western direction.
Aiṃ Aiṃ, salutation to the Mistress of the entire wheel of Kula, to the face of Vāmadeva, on the northern face.
Aiṃ Aiṃ, salutation to the Blessed One Caṇḍakapālinī, whose face is Sadyojāta; thus [to the face] facing upward.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) in this manner, and having performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the root mantra, one should perform the *kavaca* (armor) by means of the root mantra, either from the head down to the feet or from the feet up to the head. Then,
having displayed the *yonimudrā* with "Aiṃ," and having formed the *kūrmmamudrā*, [one should place it] in the heart-lotus.
One should meditate upon the Goddess in the center of the pericarp.
Meditative concentration.
She has five faces and ten arms, with full and elevated breasts;
she possesses a brilliance equal to ten million flashes of lightning, and her body is as red as vermilion.
She holds a rosary, a skull-cup, a trident, and a sword; she carries a shield, a bell, a golden noose, and a goad, while displaying the gestures of granting boons and protection from fear.
I meditate upon the Goddess Siddhilakṣmī, who has a blue neck, the moon as her crest-jewel, three eyes, and is adorned with serpents; she is the bestower of all spiritual accomplishments.
Having meditated thus, one should worship with mental offerings.
Having visualized the Goddess Kuṇḍalinī in the center of the heart-lotus, one should offer water for the feet (pādya) from the vessel to her lotus-feet. Then,
having offered water for sipping (ācamanīya), [one should visualize her] as beautiful with a bee-hive of a thousand-petaled lotus.
Having offered water for sipping from the nectar of the supreme state into the mouth, and having given the water for honor (arghya) and the water for bathing,
[one offers] sandalwood consisting of the twenty-five principles, as well as non-violence, discernment, forbearance, and compassion.

Non-attachment, non-delusion, lack of envy, lack of guile, absence of egoism, freedom from passion, sinlessness, and absence of hatred—these ten faculties are the flowers. Wind is the incense; the form of fire is the lamp; the sky is the fly-whisk; the sun is the mirror; the moon is the parasol; and the lotus is the lotus.

Having satisfied one's chosen deity with the girdle, bliss, necklaces, earrings, the unstruck sound (*anāhata-dhvani*), the bell, the nectar-essence, intellect, flesh, the mountain, and the intoxicated bees that are the dancing mind— with dances, songs, and instrumental music consisting of aesthetic flavor (*rasa*)— one becomes the essence of *rasa*.

Having offered the food offering (naivedya) and mentally recited the root mantra as many times as possible while identifying oneself with the deity, one should contemplate the deity as being fully satisfied;
thereafter, one should begin the external worship.
In this regard, one should perform the worship of Śiva according to one's own tradition.
Then follows the installation of the general arghya.
Having drawn a triangular, circular, and square mandala with water,
and having worshipped the mandala with "Oṃ, salutation to the mandala," one should place the support (ādhāra) there;
then, having worshipped the support with "Hrīṃ, salutation to the Support-Energy (Ādhāraśakti)," [one should worship] with the root mantra.

Having filled [the vessel] with pure water, having cast in perfume, flowers, unbroken rice, and so forth with the root mantra, and having prepared the *tīrtha* with the syllable *kroṃ* using the *aṅkuśa-mudrā*, [one recites]:
*aiṃ oṃ paramahaṃsini hṛdayāya*.
Having worshipped the six limbs in sequence beginning with *namaḥ*,
one should transform [the offering] into nectar by means of the *dhenumudrā* while reciting *vaṃ*, veil it with *hūṃ*, and recite the root mantra eight times.
Then, one should sprinkle oneself at the base [of the deity] with that water.
Now follows the placement of the *arghya* for the *vikheṣa*.

There, between the self and the deity, having drawn a mandala consisting of a triangle, a hexagon, a circle, and a square provided with four gates using the general *arghya* water, one should worship the center of the triangle with the root mantra. Then, in the first corner of the triangle, [one should place] "Oṃ Śrīṃ Namaḥ"; in the second corner, "Oṃ Hrīṃ Namaḥ."
In the third corner, having worshipped with "Oṃ Hūṃ Namaḥ," and having worshipped the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅgāni) in the hexagon,
one should worship the mandala with "Aiṃ Maṇḍalāya Namaḥ."

Having established the base with "Aiṃ Maṃ, salutation to the base of the arghya vessel, whose self is the circle of fire consisting of ten kalās," and having worshipped it with "Hrīṃ, salutation to the Support-Energy (Ādhāraśakti)," one should worship the ten kalās of fire therein.
Aiṁ yaṁ to Dhūmrā; aiṁ raṁ to Nīlā; aiṁ laṁ to Kapilā;
aiṁ vaṁ to Sphuliṅginī; aiṁ śaṁ to Jvālinī; aiṁ ṣaṁ to Haimavatī;
aiṁ saṁ to Havyavahā; aiṁ haṁ to Kavyavahā; aiṁ laṁ to Rātri.
Having worshipped with "Aiṃ Kṣaṃ Saṃkarṣiṇyai," one should wash the vessel with "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ Phaṭ," place it upon the support (ādhāra),
and [worship] with "Aiṃ Hrīṃ."

Having worshipped with "Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ Aṃ, obeisance to the vessel of *arghya* for the solar mandala consisting of twelve digits," one should worship the twelve digits of the Sun there in a circular form.
Aiṃ kaṃ bhaṃ to Tapinī; Aiṃ khaṃ baṃ to Tāpinī; Aiṃ gaṃ phaṃ to Dhūmrā; Aiṃ ghaṃ paṃ to Marīci; Aiṃ ṅaṃ naṃ to Jvālinī; Aiṃ caṃ dhaṃ to Ruci;
Aiṃ chaṃ daṃ to Suṣumnā; Aiṃ jaṃ thaṃ to Bhogadā; Aiṃ jhaṃ taṃ to Viśvā.
Aiṁ Ñaṁ Ṇaṁ, obeisance to Bodhinī; Aiṁ Ḍhaṁ Ṭaṁ, obeisance to Dhāriṇī; Aiṁ Ṭhaṁ Ḍaṁ, obeisance to Kṣamā.
Having thus worshipped them and filled [the vessel] with water using the root mantra,

Having worshipped with "Aiṃ Oṃ, salutation to the lunar orb, whose essence consists of sixteen digits, the nectar of the offering," one should worship the sixteen digits of the moon there in a circular form.
Aiṃ Aṃ, to Amṛtā; Aiṃ Āṃ, to Mānadā; Aiṃ Iṃ, to Pūṣā; Aiṃ Īṃ, to Tuṣṭi; Aiṃ Uṃ, to Puṣṭi; Aiṃ Ūṃ, to Rati; Aiṃ Ṛṃ, to Dhṛti; Aiṃ Ṝṃ, to Śaśinī;
Aiṃ Ḷṃ, to Candrikā; Aiṃ Ḹṃ, to Kāntā; Aiṃ Eṃ, to Jyotsnā; Aiṃ Aiṃ, to Śrī.
Aiṁ Oṃ, to Prīti; Aiṁ Auṃ, to Aṅgadā; Aiṁ Aṃ, to Pūrṇā; Aiṁ Aḥ, to Pūrṇāmṛtā—having thus worshipped, one should invoke the *tīrtha* with the *aṅkuśa-mudrā* while reciting "Kroṃ," and [then] "Vaṃ."

Having rendered [the substance] nectar-like with the *dhenumudrā*, having veiled it with "Hūṃ," having covered it with the *matsyamudrā* while reciting " Hrīṃ," and having displayed the *yonimudrā* while reciting "Aiṃ," one should worship the six limbs beginning with "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ Oṃ Paramahaṃsini, obeisance to the heart (*hṛdayāya namaḥ*)," and so forth; then, in the center, one should offer obeisance to the Self with "Haṃ Saḥ Ātmane Namaḥ."

Having worshipped with "hasakṣamalavarayūṃ ānandabhairavāya vaṣaṭ namaḥ" and "hasakṣamalavarayīṃ sudhādevyai vauṣaṭ namaḥ," one should worship the five jewels (pañcaratna) in the sequence starting from the east.
Aiṃ glūṃ, salutation to the jewels of the sky.
Aiṃ slūṃ, salutation to the jewels of heaven. Aiṃ plūṃ, salutation to the jewels of the netherworld.

Having worshipped in the center with "Aiṃ mlūṃ, obeisance to the Matyaratnas" and "Aiṃ nlūṃ, obeisance to the Nāgaratnas," and having recited the root mantra eight times, one should invoke the Goddess there, worship her with the five offerings excluding the food offering (naivedya),
recite the root mantra ten times, and offer the recitation.

Having displayed the *yonimudrā* with the syllable *aiṃ*, one should contemplate that water as being composed of Brahman. Placing a small amount of that water into the general *arghya* vessel, one should sprinkle oneself three times with that water using the root mantra (*mūlamantra*).
Then, having sprinkled the articles of worship three times with that water using the root mantra, one should gaze upon them again with the root mantra.

Having sprinkled [the water] three times with "phaṭ," having struck it with "phaṭ," having sprinkled it again with "hūṃ," having rendered it nectar with the *dhenumudrā* while reciting "vaṃ," having veiled it with "hūṃ," and having displayed the *yonimudrā* with "aiṃ," one should contemplate everything as being composed of Brahman.
Then, according to the procedure for the general *arghya*, one should place the vessels for the *pādya* and other offerings.
Then, one should perform the worship of the pedestal (pīṭhapūjā) either at the yantra or in the maṇḍala.
Now follows the worship of the seats (pīṭhapūjā).
To the north of the pedestal, from the northwest to the northeast, one should worship the lineage of gurus.
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Khphreṁ Hsauṁ, salutations to the venerable Gurus.

Aiṁ, salutations to the supreme Gurus. Aiṁ, [salutations] to the higher and lower Gurus. Aiṁ, [salutations] to the supreme preceptors. Aiṁ, [salutations] to the divine lineages. Aiṁ, [salutations] to the perfected lineages.
Aiṃ, salutations to the multitudes of human beings.
Then, in the center of the seat.
Aiṁ, to the Support-Power (Ādhāraśakti); Aiṁ, to the Tortoise (Kūrma); Aiṁ, to Śeṣa; Aiṁ, to the Earth (Pṛthivī);

Aiṁ, to the Ocean of Milk (Kṣīrasamudra); Aiṁ, to the White Island (Śvetadvīpa); Aiṁ, to the Pavilion of Jewels (Maṇimaṇḍapa); Aiṁ, to the Wish-Fulfilling Tree (Kalpavṛkṣa); Aiṁ, to the Jewel Altar (Maṇivedikā); Aiṁ, to the Lion Throne of Gems (Ratnasiṃhāsana).
In the southeast: *aiṃ* to Dharma; in the southwest: *aiṃ* to Jñāna; in the northwest: *aiṃ* to Vairāgya;
in the northeast: *aiṃ* to Aiśvarya. In the four directions starting from the east:
*aiṃ* to Adharma; *aiṃ* to Ajñāna; *aiṃ* to Avairāgya.
Aiṃ, for the absence of sovereignty. Again, in the center: Aiṃ, to Ananta; Aiṃ, to Padma;
Aiṃ Aṃ, to the solar orb consisting of twelve kalās; Aiṃ Uṃ, to the lunar orb consisting of sixteen kalās; Aiṃ Maṃ, to the fiery orb consisting of ten kalās.
Aiṃ Saṃ to the Sattva; Aiṃ Raṃ to the Rajas; Aiṃ Taṃ to the Tamas; Aiṃ Āṃ to the Self (Ātman);
Aiṃ Aṃ to the Inner Self (Antarātman); Aiṃ Paṃ to the Supreme Self (Paramātman); Aiṃ Hrīṃ to the Self of Knowledge (Jñānātman).
[These are worshipped] with the three [syllables] above, starting from the east and so forth.
Aiṃ to Jayā; Aiṃ to Vijayā; Aiṃ to Ajitā; Aiṃ to Aparājitā;
Aiṃ to Nityā; Aiṃ to Vilāsinī; Aiṃ to Dogdhrī; Aiṃ to Aghorā;
in the center, Aiṃ to Maṅgalā; above that, Aiṃ Hsauṃḥ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ to Sadāśiva.
"To the seat of the great preta. Then, one should perform the visualization of the form upon the yantra:

"Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Sauḥ, I visualize the form of the goddess Śrī Siddhilakṣmī; obeisance. Having thus visualized the form, one should invoke the goddess into it, meditating on the goddess there as before.

Having formed the *yonimudrā* with the syllable *aiṃ*, and having recited the root mantra while holding a handful of flowers, one should invoke the Goddess in the form of light through the flowing nostril,
saying: *hrīṃ śrīṃ*, "O You who abide within the great forest of lotuses, whose body is supreme bliss!"
O Mother who destroys all beings, come indeed, O Supreme Goddess!
Having thus invoked: *Aiṃ*, Goddess Siddhilakṣmī, come here!
*Aiṃ*, Goddess Siddhi, stay here! *Aiṃ*, Goddess Siddhi, be present here!
*Aiṃ*, Goddess Siddhi, remain firmly established here! *Aiṃ*, Goddess Siddhi, face me here!
Having performed the ritual of sakalīkaraṇa with the six-limbed mantra beginning with "Aiṃ Oṃ Paramahaṃsini, obeisance to the heart," and so forth;
having veiled [the deity] with "Hūṃ"; having rendered [it] nectar with the cow-mudrā (dhenumudrā) using "Vaṃ";
having displayed the yoni-mudrā with "Aiṃ"; and having thus displayed the mudrās for invocation and the others.
One should perform the rite of vitalization (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*):
*Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ, the vital breaths of Śrī Siddhilakṣmī are here as vital breaths;
Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ, the life-force (*jīva*) of Śrī Siddhilakṣmī is established here.*
Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ! O Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, may your speech, mind, eyes, lineage, nose, vital breaths, and all your sense faculties come here and remain happily for a long time—svāhā!
Having thus performed the consecration of the vital breaths (prāṇapratiṣṭhā), one should touch the deity with the hand and recite the root mantra three times.

Then, having recited the root mantra and joined his palms in añjali, saying "O Goddess Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, forgive me," he should perform the act of supreme unification (paramīkaraṇa) and sprinkle the Goddess three times with the water from the special arghya vessel while reciting the root mantra.
Then, one should worship with offerings according to one's ability.

Having recited the root mantra and offered the seat in the form of a handful of flowers with the words, "I worship this seat and the venerable sandals of the goddess Śrī Siddhilakṣmī; obeisance," one should offer water with the words, "I present this seat to the goddess Śrī Siddhilakṣmī; obeisance."
In every ritual service, one should likewise offer the arghya water in this very manner.
Then, having recited the root mantra, one should offer a welcome with the words: "O Goddess Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, you are welcome."
To the goddess Mūla Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, this is the water for the feet; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance!
Oṃ, this is the arghya for the Root Śrī Devī; to the Śrī Pādukā, svāhā!
Oṃ, this is the ācamanīya for the Root Śrī Devī; to the Śrī Pādukā, svadhā!
Oṃ, this madhuparka is for the root Śrī Devī; to the feet of Śrī, svāhā!
To the Root Śrī Devī, this water for sipping; to the Śrīpādukā, nectar.
To the Root Śrī Devī, this water for bathing; to the Śrīpādukā, obeisance.
O Śrī Devī, this sandalwood fragrance is for the venerable sandals.
To the Root Śrī Devī, this red sandalwood [paste] for the venerable sandals.
To the Root Śrī Devī, this sindūra for the venerable sandals.
To the Root Śrī Devī, this flower: *śrīpādukā* vauṣaṭ.
Then, with the root mantra, offer three handfuls of flowers: "O Śrī Devī, I worship the Śrī Pādukā; obeisance!"
Then, having offered five handfuls of flowers to the Goddess on her head, heart, middle body, feet, and all over her limbs, and having uttered the root mantra,
one should request permission by saying, "I worship from your enclosure; please command me," and then perform the worship of the enclosure (āvaraṇapūjā).
One should perform [it].
One should worship the six limbs with the mantra "aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ hsauṃ oṃ paramahaṃsini hṛdayāya namaḥ" and so forth, at the southeast, northeast, center, and in the cardinal directions.

Then, on the outer square, starting from the east: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ Indrāya namaḥ | Aiṃ Agnaye | Aiṃ Yamāya | Aiṃ Nairṛtaye | Aiṃ Varuṇāya | Aiṃ Vāyave | Aiṃ Kuberāya | Aiṃ Īśānāya | Aiṃ...
To Brahmā above; Aiṃ, to Ananta below.
Then, in the center: *Aiṃ Kṣāṃ*, obeisance to Śrī Kṣetrapāla.
Having recited the root mantra, one should worship the Root Goddess together with Kṣetrapāla, saying: "Obeisance, I worship the venerable sandals of the goddess Śrī Siddhilakṣmī.
Thus one should worship the Root Goddess accompanied by Kṣetrapāla.
Then, at the southern gate.
Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Gaṇapatinātha; Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Gaṇapativallabhāmbā.
At the western gate.
Aiṁ, the venerable sandals of the Lord Kṣetrapāla Valotkaṭa;
Aiṁ, the venerable sandals of the Mother Vallabhāmbā, the beloved consort of Kṣetrapāla Valotkaṭa, who is the destroyer of all.
At the northern gate.
Aiṁ, the venerable sandals of Vaṭukanātha; aiṁ, the venerable sandals of Vaṭukanāthavallabhāmbā.
At the eastern gate.
Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Siddhiyoginī; Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Oṃkāranātha;
Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Vṛkṣasaṃkaṭanātha; Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Mahākaravīraśmaśānanātha.
Then, in the eastern street.
From Īśāna to the southeast: Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Śrī Vīranātha.
Aiṁ, the venerable sandals of Daśakaṇṭhanātha; Aiṁ, the venerable sandals of Vasiṣṭhanātha; Aiṁ, the venerable sandals of Śrī Jayadrathanātha—on the southern path.
Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of the goddess Mataṅgī together with the deity Kaṅkāla;
Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of the goddess Vīrāvalī,
in the western path.
Aiṁ, the venerable sandals of Tribhuvananātha; Aiṁ, the venerable sandals of Siddhinātha;
Aiṁ, the venerable sandals of Khaḍganātha—on the northern path.
Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Ānandanātha; Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Nityānandanātha;
in the northeast.
Aiṃ Jaṃ, the venerable sandals of the goddess Jambhinī.
In the southeast.
Aiṃ Taṃ, the venerable sandals of the goddess Stambhinī.
In the southwest.
Aiṃ Māṃ, the venerable sandals of the goddess Mohinī.
In the northwest.
Aiṃ Āṃ, the venerable sandals of the goddess Ākarṣiṇī.
On the eight petals, the worship of Brahmāṇī and the others.
Then, on the twelve petals.

Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Śivādevī. Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Bhagavatīdevī. Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Māyādevī. Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Bhadrādevī. Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Kini Kini Devī. Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of Vimalādevī.
Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of the goddess Yamajihvā; Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of the goddess Dakṣiṇī, who is the skin-clad one;
Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of the goddess Ghaṇṭodarī; Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of the goddess Caulamātā;
Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of the goddess Śrīkiṅkiṇī; Aiṃ, the venerable sandals of the goddess Śrīkākini.
The twelve-petaled worship.
Then, on an eight-petalled [lotus].
Aiṃ Aṃ, the venerable sandals of Brahmāṇī together with Asitāṅga Bhairava; Aiṃ Kaṃ, the venerable sandals of Māheśvarī together with Ruru Bhairava;
Aiṃ Caṃ, the venerable sandals of Kaumārī together with Caṇḍa Bhairava.
Aiṃ Ṭaṃ, the venerable sandals of Vaiṣṇavī together with Krodhabhairava. Aiṃ Taṃ, the venerable sandals of Vārāhī together with Unmattabhairava.
Aiṃ Paṃ, the venerable sandals of Indrāṇī together with Kapālībhairava.
Aiṁ Yaṁ, the venerable sandals of Cāmuṇḍā together with Bhīṣaṇabhairava; Aiṁ Śaṁ, the venerable sandals of Mahālakṣmī together with Saṃhārabhairava.
Then, in the three verses:
Aiṃ, salutation to the reality of the Self for the pacification of internal suffering.
Aiṃ, salutation to the principle of Vidyā for the pacification of suffering pertaining to the elemental realm.
Aiṃ, salutation to the Śiva-tattva for the pacification of afflictions pertaining to the divine realm.
Then, in the six corners, starting from the east:
Aiṁ Ḍāṁ, the venerable sandals of Ḍākinī; Aiṁ Rāṁ, the venerable sandals of Rākini;
Aiṁ Lāṁ, the venerable sandals of Lākini; Aiṁ Kāṁ, the venerable sandals of Kākini;
Aiṁ Śāṁ, the venerable sandals of Śākini; Aiṁ Hāṁ, the venerable sandals of Hākini.
Then, in the right corner of the triangle.
Aiṃ Jaṃ, salutation to the sacred seat of Jālandhara, together with the power of Brāhmī.
In the left corner.
Aiṃ Yūṃ, salutation to the Pīṭha of Pūrṇagiri, accompanied by the Śakti Vaiṣṇavī.
In the upper corner.
Aiṃ Kāṃ, salutation to the seat of Kāmarūpa, together with the power Maudrī.
Above the triangle.
Aiṃ Oṃ, salutation to the sacred seat of Oḍḍiyāna, together with the Guardian of the Field (Kṣetrapāla).
Then, one should worship the Root Goddess with three handfuls of flowers while reciting the root mantra.
Then, taking the special *arghya* water, [one should recite]:

"Aiṃ! In the wheel consisting of all bliss, may the Goddess Śrī Siddhilakṣmī—the Blessed Lady who is the essence of all mantras and principles, Parāparāmbā—along with her weapons, her vehicle, her limbs, and her retinue, be present through the Parāpara [state]."

"May she, honored with worship, gratified, and fully satisfied, protect me; Svāhā!"— with these words, one should offer water for the arghya, unbroken grains (akṣata), and flowers into the hand of the Goddess.

Then, having offered three handfuls of flowers with the root mantra, one should perform the libation three times with the special arghya water, saying: "With the root mantra, I satiate the goddess Śrī Siddhilakṣmī—along with her weapons, her vehicle, her limbs, and her retinue—and the venerable pādukā; namaḥ svāhā."
Then, with the root mantra, having worshipped the Śrī Devī— along with her weapons, her vehicle, her limbs, and her retinue—
with three handfuls of flowers while reciting "I worship, I bow" (pūjayāmi namaḥ) three times,
one should display the Yoni-mudrā while uttering "Aiṃ."
Then, one should perform the worship of the deity according to the sequence of one's own tradition.
Then follows the offering of incense and so forth.
Saying *phaṭ*, sprinkle the incense vessel with the water from the general *arghya* offering;
then worship it with perfume, flowers, and unbroken rice grains, saying: *hrīṃ dhūpabhājanāya namaḥ*.
Then, worship the bell with perfume and other offerings, saying: *hrīṃ jaya dhvanimantramātaḥ svāhā*.
Having offered incense, displaying the *dhenumudrā* while reciting "vaṃ," veiling [the offering] with "hūṃ," and having recited the root mantra ten times, one should ring the bell with the left hand,
hold the incense vessel with the index finger and thumb, and utter the root mantra.
This is the incense for the venerable Goddess, for the venerable sandals.
Produced from the sap of the lord of the forest, rich in fragrance, the most excellent scent—
to be inhaled by all the gods, may this incense be accepted.
In the same manner, having thoroughly cleansed and worshipped the lamp-vessel, [one should offer] this root-lamp to the Śrī Devī at the feet of Śrī.
This great lamp, brilliantly radiant, dispelling darkness everywhere,
a light both internal and external— may this lamp be accepted.
Then, having offered three handfuls of flowers with the root mantra, having brought the food offering (naivedya),

having sprinkled it with the water of the *arghya* while reciting "phaṭ," having protected it with the wheel-mudrā while reciting "hrīṃ," having turned it into nectar with the cow-mudrā while reciting "vaṃ," having veiled it with "hūṃ," and having displayed the womb-mudrā with "aiṃ."
Having recited the root mantra eight times, one should offer this food offering (naivedya), together with its accessories, to the venerable Goddess by means of the root mantra at the feet of Śrī.
O Supreme Goddess, please accept this divine, well-prepared supreme rice-offering contained in a golden vessel, consisting of five types and endowed with the six flavors.

Having thus announced with the root mantra, and having offered this water for sipping (*ācamanīya*) to the Śrī Devī with the mantra "Śrīpādukā sudhā," [he offers] the root mantra; then he offers this betel (*tāmbūla*) to the Śrī Devī with the mantra "Śrīpādukā."
One should satisfy them three times as before.
Having offered three handfuls of flowers with the root mantra,
one should display the yoni-mudrā while reciting "Aiṃ."

Then, the offering of the *bali*: having drawn a mandala consisting of a triangle, a circle, and a square, and having worshipped it with "Aiṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to the all-pervading mandala," [one recites]:
"Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ, O Root Goddess Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, accept this sacrificial offering (*pūjā-bali*)."
Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Then follows the offering to the spirits (*bhūtabali*). Having worshipped the mandala as before, [one recites]:
*aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ khphreṃ hsauṃ oṃ hrīṃ sarvavighnakṛdbhyaḥ sarvabhūtebhyo hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*.
Then, the offering for Vaṭuka and the others.
Having drawn a triangular-circular mandala in the northeast and having worshipped the mandala with "Vāṃ, obeisance to Vaṭuka," [one should proceed].
Hrīṃ! Come, come, O Son of the Goddess, Vaṭukanātha, radiant with the mass of your tawny matted locks, three-eyed, flame-mouthed one!
Destroy all obstacles; accept this bali-offering along with all ritual services, svāhā!
Then, one should display the mudrā of the thumb and ring finger.
Then, in the northwest: having worshipped the mandala with "Yāṃ yoginībhyaḥ namaḥ," [one recites] "Hrīṃ!
Whether above the cosmic egg, or in the expanse of the sky, on the surface of the earth, or in the partless [space]..."

Whether in the netherworld or in fire, in wind or water, or wherever they may dwell— whether in sacred fields, seats, or secondary seats— may the goddesses, who have established their feet there and are pleased by incense,
lamps, meat, and the ritual of the auspicious *bali* offering, always protect us; for they are worthy of worship by the lords of heroes (*vīrendra*).
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ Yāṃ, to all the Yoginīs, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
One should display the mudrā in the shape of a vulva with the left thumb, index, middle, and ring fingers;
then, having worshipped the mandala in the southwest with "Kṣāṃ, obeisance to Kṣetrapāla," one should proceed.
KṢĀṂ KṢĪṂ KṢŪṂ KṢAIṂ KṢAUṂ KṢAḤ, O Kṣetrapāla, accept this offering, svāhā!
Having made the index finger of the left fist straight like an arrow, one should display the mudrā.
In the southeast: having worshipped the mandala with "Gāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati," [one recites]:
"Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaiṃ Gauṃ Gaḥ, O Gaṇapati, bestower of excellent boons, bring all people under my control; accept this offering, svāhā!"
Khphreṃ! Śivā Bhagavatī, as well as Māyā and Bhadrā; Kiṃkiṇī and Vimalā, Yamajihvā and Karṣaṇī.
May Ghaṇṭodarī, Cauramātā, Kiṅkiṇī, Kākinī,
and Siddhilakṣmī always accept the offering on the thirteenth lunar day.
For the destruction of all obstacles and the warding off of all enemies,
may the fortune of success be yours eternally, fulfilling all desires.
O Goddess Siddhilakṣmī, accept this worship and offering; hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Having formed the left fist with the middle finger positioned like a tooth, one should display the mudrā.
Then follows the offering of the *ārātrika* lamp.

Having drawn an eight-petaled lotus with sandalwood paste in a vessel made of gold or other precious materials, having lit a lamp, having sprinkled [the offering] while reciting *phaṭ*, having rendered it nectar by means of the *dhenu-mudrā* while reciting *vaṃ*, having veiled it while reciting *hūṃ*, and having displayed the *yoni-mudrā* while reciting *aiṃ*, one should worship it with perfume and other offerings while reciting *hrīṃ namaḥ*. Then, [recite] *śrīṃ hrīṃ glūṃ*.
Having worshipped again with *sluṃ mluṃ pluṃ nluṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ mūlaṃ*, and having purified the root mantra eight times,
one should lift it up with the right hand while ringing the bell with the left hand; then, reciting the root mantra, one should perform the *nīrājana* nine times.
O Goddess, surrounded by the entire assembly of deities and the lords of all mandalas,
O Sovereign of the World, accept this *ārātrika* offering.
Then, one should display the wheel mudrā with the syllable *hrīṃ*.
Then, having visualized the deity as gracious and propitiated her with mental offerings, one should offer five handfuls of flowers and perform the recitation.
Now, the procedure for recitation (japa).

Having performed the breath control (prāṇāyāma) and other rites, as well as the assignment of the seers (ṛṣi) and the six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa) with the root mantra, one should meditate upon the deity in the heart and perform the purification of the tongue.
*Śrīṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ*—on the tongue is *Dīpinī*. *Aiṃ vada vada vāgvādini oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ klinne kledini hāṃ phreṃ kṣauṃ mahāmokṣaṃ kuru kroṃ namaḥ*—on the tongue.
"Krīṃ hūṃ strīṃ hūṃ phaṭ"—this is the *kullukā*, which one places upon the head.
Reciting "Krīṃ," one should establish a barrier at the throat; reciting "Oṃ," one should establish a barrier at the heart.

*Klīṃ*— thus [one worships] Kākinī at the place called the base of the *liṅga*. *Oṃ aṃ mūlaṃ aiṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ.*
Śaṃ, ṣaṃ, saṃ, haṃ, laṃ, kṣaṃ, oṃ—thus [are the syllables] in the Maṇipūra at the navel.
Aiṃ: the Yonimudrā at the Mūlādhāra. Oṃ Mū Oṃ: thus is the warding off of the two sons.
Meditation on the mantra.
One should contemplate the entire Vidyā, from the base to the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra),
resembling ten million suns and previously beheld by yogis;
indeed, one should conceive with the intellect the oneness of the deity, the guru, and the mantra.
Having done thus, and having taken up the rosary,
one should worship it with "Aiṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the Akṣamālikā," and then, reflecting on the meaning of the mantra in the mind, meditate upon the deity in the heart.

One should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times or one thousand times. Again, having performed breath control (prāṇāyāma), the assignment of the seer and so forth (ṛṣyādi), and the ritual placement on the hands and limbs (karāṅganyāsa), and having recited the limb-mantras (aṅgamantra) seven times,
one should recite first and then recite afterwards seven times in sequence.

Then, having placed the special *arghya* water, joined with flowers, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and so forth, in his right hand, he should offer the recitation (*japa*) in the form of light into the hand of the Goddess.
Oṃ! O secret one, protector of secrets from the beginning, accept this recitation performed by us;
may accomplishment be mine, O Goddess, through your grace, O Great Sovereign.
Having thus offered the recitation (*japa*), presented three handfuls of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*),
recited the hymns, armor-mantras (*kavaca*), the thousand names (*sahasranāma*), and so forth, performed prostrations such as the staff-prostration (*daṇḍapraṇāma*),
and having paid homage with the *aiṃ* syllable using the *yonimudrā*, one should pray to the deity.
One should present the worship to the Goddess with the special arghya water.

Oṃ! From this point forward, whatever has been thought by the mind, spoken by speech, or performed by action— with the hands, feet, belly, or genitals— throughout the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, by virtue of my life-force, intellect, body, and authority over dharma, may all that be an offering unto Brahman.
I offer my own ritual action at the lotus feet of the goddess Śrī Siddhilakṣmī; homage!
Then, having offered the special *arghya* water and whirled it above the deity, one should contemplate everything as dissolved into the Goddess;
then, releasing the deities into the heart with the *saṃhāra-mudrā*, and having performed the *prāṇāma* and other rites, one should draw a triangular circle within a mandala in the northeast.

Having offered the *nirmālya* with the mantra: "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Khphreṃ Hsauṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ! Salutation to the one who dwells in the place of the *nirmālya*, to Ucchiṣṭacāṇḍālī," one should worship her with perfumes and other offerings.
Then, having performed the ritual sipping (ācamana) with the water from the Goddess’s feet and so forth, [one should offer] sandalwood, flowers, and other items to the Goddess.
